{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZbw6nA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDDBTg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 45, "title": "Schedule automatic OAM address reload at H=10 on the first VBlank line", "body": "## Problem

Issue #43 added automatic OAM address reload, but schedules it at the beginning of VBlank. Its own [specification record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/11e4c0ba10893f10f1a0caec9f461620a37f3adc/docs/issue-43-validation.md#disagreements-and-bounded-approximation) attributes the detailed Fullsnes event to **V=225, H=10 dots**. The current H=0 implementation can change OAM reads, write-pair phase and priority rotation during the intervening 40 master clocks.

This is a bounded follow-up to an incomplete timing fix identified in the latest assessment. The supplied context lists no open duplicate Issue.

## Expected outcome

Implement the documented automatic reload as a distinct raster event. For the currently supported NTSC, non-overscan model:

- VBlank begins at V=225, H=0; automatic OAM reload occurs at H=10 dots, corresponding to 40 master clocks under the existing coordinate model.
- When forced blank is clear at the reload event, restore the programmed nine-bit OAM word address from `$2102/$2103`. Both existing address cursors become `2 * (($2103 & 1) * 256 + $2102)`, selecting even byte phase.
- When forced blank remains set across the event, suppress automatic reload.
- Fire once per frame, including when one clock-advance call crosses the event or several scanlines. Normal accesses after the event must advance the cursor without another reload.
- Preserve the existing data-latch retention policy, explicitly labeled as policy rather than independently verified hardware behavior.

The automatic event must remain distinct from address-register writes and the separately documented first-VBlank-line INIDISP behavior.

### Specification basis and qualifications

Use [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), specifically **SNES Timing H/V Events**, **SNES Memory OAM Access**, and **INIDISP**, together with [Anomie's Register Doc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), specifically **OAMADDL/H**, **INIDISP**, and **SPRITES/OAM**.

The repository records Fullsnes v1.5 SHA-256 `3853b65a7331bf12eea431ff494a2948a1c78ef22f7e819db4b139fd5a79f6c6` and Anomie revision 1157 SHA-256 `19dfdf3f1c206655b8ede11bcd6dc053e36634f876819e40bb39cfb88a237dfd` in its [source table](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/11e4c0ba10893f10f1a0caec9f461620a37f3adc/docs/issue-43-validation.md#specification-record-written-before-production-changes).

Reconcile the detailed H=10 event with the general descriptions of reload at VBlank beginning before coding. Correct the earlier H=0 contract and its tests using that evidence. If examination of the cited specifications contradicts the recorded event, document the discrepancy and derive the corrected bounded contract; do not preserve or replace requirements solely to satisfy existing tests.

This planning pass inspected repository evidence only. The raw specifications are absent from this checkout and were not independently fetched. Physical forced-blank latency and coincident bus strobes remain unresolved; assertions about immediate INIDISP effects and access-completion ordering must identify their model assumptions.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `11e4c0ba10893f10f1a0caec9f461620a37f3adc`.

[`SystemBus::tick`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/11e4c0ba10893f10f1a0caec9f461620a37f3adc/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L164) calls `oam_scanline_start` immediately after incrementing V. [`Ppu::oam_scanline_start`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/11e4c0ba10893f10f1a0caec9f461620a37f3adc/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs#L88) reloads immediately for line 225.

To reproduce, initialize distinct OAM sentinel pairs during forced blank, retain a cursor different from the programmed reload address, enable display, and advance naturally through V=225/H=0 and H=40. Current code restores the address at H=0. Expected behavior restores it at H=40.

Existing [machine OAM vectors](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/11e4c0ba10893f10f1a0caec9f461620a37f3adc/crates/snes-core/src/machine/ppu_oam_tests.rs) cover VBlank entry and DMA boundaries but encode the H=0 convention. The [original CPU guest](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/11e4c0ba10893f10f1a0caec9f461620a37f3adc/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_oam_access.rs) observes reload after polling VBlank; it does not distinguish these two event placements.

Scope is the automatic reload event, affected OAM tests, and necessary documentation. CGRAM arbitration, rendering-owned corruption addresses, object-fetch timing, forced-blank electrical latency, disputed INIDISP transitions, PAL, overscan and interlace remain separate work. No general raster pipeline or scheduler rewrite is required.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the specification reconciliation, exact sections/version, chosen event and remaining uncertainties. Explicitly supersede Issue #43's H=0 automatic-reload convention.
- [ ] Implement the distinct reload event through normal device-clock advancement. Demonstrate no automatic reload at H=0, one reload at H=40, suppression with forced blank held throughout, and recurrence in a subsequent frame.
- [ ] Add original numerical unit vectors at H=38/40/42 and across H=0. Assert both cursors, even phase, programmed address and retained latch. Compare a single advance with partitioned advances crossing the same event; also cover an advance spanning line boundaries. Expected values must not call production reload helpers.
- [ ] Add naturally timed CPU and forward/reverse DMA accesses around H=40. Verify source sampling versus destination commitment when the event falls between them, address/count progression, pair effects and absence of duplicate reload. Keep H=0 access-availability tests distinct from H=40 reload tests. Label coincident-access ordering as model behavior where physical timing is unverified.
- [ ] Add an original, bounded 65C816 guest that distinguishes H=0 from H=40 using executed synchronization and OAM accesses. Derive its access windows explicitly; for example, perform an early-VBlank read before H=40 and observe the restored programmed address afterward. Assert source-backed post-reload results independently of arbitrary rendering-corruption bytes. The host supplies only the cartridge and observes results/deadlines. Document original MIT code/data provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Show at least one focused numerical test and the guest failing on the baseline and passing after the correction. Update obsolete H=0 expectations with explained derivations; preserve other OAM latch, mirror, rotation, DMA/HDMA and game regression coverage.
- [ ] Pass the following existing gates and the new focused tests, recording commands and actual outcomes:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
(cd web && npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds')
```

Use the README's documented compiler selection or alternate browser port when applicable. Preserve fixture pins, hashes, licenses, replay inputs, durations and assertions, including Castle's complete route and Memory's audio/gameplay checks. Acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.

- [ ] Update README and validation evidence. Keep `ppu-ports` and `scheduler` partial and retain all 24 inventory categories and their outstanding scope. Remaining port work includes CGRAM arbitration, VRAM invalid-fetch values, OAM corruption/fetch behavior, blanking latency, external counter inputs and physical reset retention. Passing these bounded checks establishes neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

Additional original CPU guests exercising independently documented forced-blank transitions near the reload event. Unresolved electrical timing must remain explicitly unverified.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
